sum: The classic walk from Lukla through Namche, Tengboche and Dingboche to Everest Base Camp and the Kala Patthar viewpoint, with two built-in acclimatization days.

guide.note: Khumbu has not enforced the national guide requirement, so independent trekking remains possible here. A licensed guide still earns their fee on this route: they book beds above Dingboche, watch for altitude symptoms and arrange help quickly if you need to descend.

access: Fly to Lukla from Kathmandu or, in the peak months, from Manthali in Ramechhap. Flights go early in the morning and stop when cloud or wind builds, so delays of a day are common.

photo.a: Everest's dark summit pyramid stands behind its white west shoulder, with the sharp snow peak of Nuptse to the right and the Khumbu glacier along the valley floor.
photo.c: Everest, Nuptse and the Khumbu glacier from Kala Patthar

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Sagarmatha park and Khumbu municipality permits
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
airport transfers; Kathmandu hotel nights in some packages

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park gate in Monjo, or in advance at the park counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry permit
permits.where: At the municipality's tourist information centre in Lukla when you land, or at the Monjo checkpoint if you walk in from the road. It cannot be bought in Kathmandu.

transportText: Flights to Lukla and back, from Kathmandu or (in the busy months) from Manthali with a night drive to the airstrip
tips: Carry enough cash from Kathmandu or Namche; there are no working ATMs above Namche.
Walk slower than feels necessary on the way up. Arriving fresh matters more than arriving first.
Drink three to four litres a day and treat all water with tablets, a filter or UV.
Hot showers, charging and Wi-Fi cost extra at every lodge and get pricier with height.
Use the Dingboche rest day to check how you feel with the altitude self-check before committing to Lobuche.

days.t: Fly to Lukla, walk to Phakding
days.note: After the morning flight, an easy and mostly downhill walk along the Dudh Koshi. Sleeping lower than Lukla is a gentle start for your body.
Permits are checked at the park gate in Monjo. After the high Hillary bridge the trail climbs about 600 m without a break; take it slowly and drink plenty.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Walk up to the ridge above town for a first look at Everest, loop through Khumjung if you feel good, then come back down to sleep at the same height.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: A level balcony trail with Ama Dablam ahead, then a drop to the river at Phunki Tenga and a steady two-hour forest climb to the monastery.
The trees thin out after Pangboche and the valley opens. This is the biggest sleeping gain of the trek so far, so arrive unhurried and keep the afternoon quiet.
Climb the ridge behind the village as far as feels comfortable, then descend for lunch. Do not go higher tomorrow if you still have a headache this evening.
A gentle terrace walk to Thukla, a stiff climb up the terminal moraine past the climbers' memorials, then an easy stretch beside the glacier to Lobuche.

days.t: Lobuche to Gorak Shep and Everest Base Camp
days.note: Reach Gorak Shep by late morning, leave your bag and continue over rough moraine to base camp and back. A long day at altitude; turn round by early afternoon whatever point you have reached.

days.t: Kala Patthar, then down to Pheriche
days.note: A cold pre-dawn climb of about 400 m to the viewpoint, breakfast back at Gorak Shep, then a long descent. Dropping over 900 m of sleeping altitude makes the night noticeably easier.
Mostly downhill, but with the climb back up to Tengboche and another from the river to the Namche trail. Long, and harder on the knees than the map suggests.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Steeply down to the river, then the rolling valley trail and a final uphill hour into Lukla. Reconfirm tomorrow's flight when you arrive.
Morning flight to Kathmandu or Manthali, weather permitting. If flights are cancelled you wait, walk out towards the road, or share a helicopter.
